items.definition:
Change (something) fundamentally and dramatically.
The internet has revolutionized the way we communicate.

To talk rapidly and unintelligibly; to make a continuous murmuring sound.
The baby began to babble happily in its crib.

to illegally obtain money from someone by deception
He was accused of trying to defraud the insurance company.

to give someone the courage or confidence to do something
His success emboldened him to take on new challenges.

to beat (someone) with a whip or stick as punishment
Historically, sailors could be flogged for insubordination.

To make a sudden forward thrust with the body
The fencer had to lunge forward to score a point.

to think too much about something
Don't overthink it; just make a decision.

to play roughly and energetically; to win easily
The children loved to romp in the garden.

to make a soft, muffled crackling sound, as of dry leaves or paper
The dry leaves rustled underfoot as we walked through the forest.

to search for and collect (anything usable) from discarded waste
Birds often scavenge for food in urban areas.

To pay someone too little.
Many companies underpay their interns.

add something to the end of a written document
Please append your signature to the bottom of the form.

reject ownership of
The family decided to disown him after his criminal acts.

kill by electric shock
Be careful not to electrocute yourself with faulty wiring.

predict or prophesy (the future)
Ancient prophets claimed to foretell future events.

give legal or formal status to
They decided to formalize their agreement with a written contract.

shout or yell
He had to holler to be heard over the music.

take legal possession of (something)
The police decided to impound the illegally parked car.

do, use, or express to an excessive degree
Don't overdo it at the gym on your first day back.

to tremble or shake with a slight rapid motion
Her lip began to quiver as she tried to hold back tears.

to recall past experiences or events
They spent the evening reminiscing about their college days.

to adapt for use in a different purpose
We can repurpose old plastic bottles into new art projects.

to annoy or irritate
His constant complaining really began to rile me.

to make a series of soft explosive sounds
The old engine began to sputter and then died.

to pull (a tree or plant) up from the ground; to move (someone) from their home or usual environment
The strong winds uprooted several trees during the storm.

to free from guilt or blame
The court decided to absolve him of all charges.

to refuse to obey
Children should not disobey their parents.

to sit on eggs to hatch them; to develop slowly
The hen will incubate her eggs for about three weeks.

estimate to be larger or greater than it really is
Don't overestimate how much time you have to complete the task.

transfer (a business, industry, or service) from public to private ownership and control
The government decided to privatize the national railway system.

to act out a particular role or character
They often roleplay different scenarios in their training sessions.

carve (wood) into an object by repeatedly cutting small slices from it
He used a knife to whittle a piece of wood into a bird.

To encourage or assist (someone) to do something wrong, in particular, to commit a crime.
He was accused of aiding and abetting the thief.

To feed a baby with milk from the breast.
Many mothers choose to breastfeed their infants for the first year.

obtain (something) by force, threats, or other unfair means
The criminals tried to extort money from the shop owner.

lose strength or momentum; hesitate or waver
Her voice began to falter as she told the sad story.

indulge in daydreaming about something desired
He often fantasizes about winning the lottery.

grow too big for something; develop beyond a habit
My son has outgrown all his clothes.

form a theory or theories about something
Scientists continue to theorize about the origins of the universe.

to make something slightly wet; to make a feeling or reaction less strong
The rain began to dampen the ground.

put oneself into a place or situation where one is unwelcome or uninvited
I didn't mean to intrude on your private conversation.

To convert into money; to earn revenue from
Many content creators try to monetize their videos through advertising.

To last longer than; to survive
The old car managed to outlast several newer models.

To smell strongly and unpleasantly; to be strongly suggestive of something unpleasant
The garbage can began to reek after a few days in the sun.

To create and maintain a state of extreme fear in (someone)
The gang continued to terrorize the neighborhood.

urinate
It is important to urinate regularly for bladder health.

to make a vehement protest or demand
The crowd began to clamor for the speaker to address their concerns.

to mend or make shoes; to assemble roughly
They had to cobble together a plan quickly before the deadline.

to upset the stability of; to make unstable
The sudden economic downturn threatened to destabilize the entire region.

to list items
Please enumerate the reasons for your decision.

to put someone into a trance-like state
The magician claimed he could hypnotize volunteers from the audience.

to provide with insufficient or unbalanced nutrition
Lack of food can malnourish a child.

to do better than someone else
She always tries to outdo her brother in school.

annoy; irritate
It really peeves me when people are late.

consider or assess again
We need to reassess our strategy.

to roll about in mud or water; to indulge in an unrestrained way
Pigs love to wallow in the mud.

conspire; cooperate in a secret or unlawful way
The two companies were accused of colluding to fix prices.

create or devise (a story, plan, etc.)
She tried to concoct an excuse for being late.

knock or force out of position
The strong winds threatened to dislodge the roof tiles.

absorb all the attention or interest of
The book was so engrossing that I lost track of time.

twist together
The branches of the two trees began to entwine as they grew closer.

make acquainted or conversant
You should familiarize yourself with the new software before the training session.

trim something by cutting away its outer edges; reduce something in size, extent, quantity, or number
He used a small knife to pare the apple.

manufacture sections of (a building or structure) off-site, for assembly on-site
Many modern homes are prefabricated in factories to save time.
